- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 10d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7d horizon.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 3–7% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; apply early correction (day 10–15) to align with sentiment reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts when price volatility >15% from 10d average; cap forecast at ±10% of 10d moving average.
- For auctions with CAP3 EU/DE supply, model tends to overreact to auction dates; reduce forecast sensitivity to auction days by 15–20% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
